transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Yeah, um, well, the main reason I’m here is that at work—I'm a nurse—and on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. Like, an IV pump will beep, or I'll overhear someone asking another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I’ve completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was even working on. 

Speaking of call lights, they actually just installed this new system on our unit last month, and the tone it makes is just... awful. It sounds exactly like my microwave at home. I actually had to buy a new microwave recently because my old one just stopped spinning the plate, and it was a whole ordeal getting it delivered. The delivery guy couldn't find my apartment complex. They always go to the wrong building because the numbers are painted in this really weird, modern font that you can barely read from the street. I keep meaning to complain to the HOA about it, but I never remember to go to the meetings. 

But, um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, work. Yeah, I just... I can't seem to hold onto a thought with all the noise.
Do you find that you have trouble focusing or get easily distracted in situations outside of work, like at home or during conversations?

Um, outside of work? I haven't really thought about it, honestly. I guess I'm not sure. I mean, at home, I live alone... well, with my cat, Barnaby. He’s a rescue. I actually found him near the dumpsters behind that grocery store on 4th street—the one that just closed down? 

It’s a real shame they closed because they had the absolute best bakery section. Their sourdough was amazing. I tried making my own sourdough a couple years ago, like everyone else was doing, you know? But my starter died after like three days. I named it Clint Yeastwood, which I thought was so funny, but yeah, it just started smelling like nail polish remover and I had to throw the whole jar away. It was a really nice jar, too, one of those expensive glass ones with the wire latch... 

But anyway, I don't really have a lot of conversations at home since it's just me and Barnaby, so... I don't know. Did you mean like when I'm out with friends, or...? I'm sorry, I completely lost the thread of what you were asking.
Can you think of times when you're not at work—like when you're watching TV, reading, or talking with someone—where you lose focus or find your mind wandering easily?

Um, yeah, I guess... watching TV or reading? I mean, I don't read as much as I used to. I used to read constantly when I was a kid. Like, those big fantasy series? I was obsessed. I actually still have this huge box of paperbacks in my closet that I can't bring myself to get rid of. My mom keeps telling me to donate them to the library, but the library near me has these really weird hours now. They close at like 4 PM on Tuesdays, which makes zero sense because kids are just getting out of school then. 

I remember when I was in middle school, we'd go to the library every day after class and they had this librarian, Mrs. Gable, who always wore these giant, colorful glasses. Like, neon green, bright pink. She was so nice, though. She let us eat snacks in the study rooms even though it was strictly against the rules. I think about her sometimes because I saw a pair of glasses just like hers online the other day when I was trying to buy new scrubs. 

But, um... wait. You were asking about TV? I honestly can't remember the last time I sat down and just watched a show without doing something else, but I'm not really sure if that's what you mean. What were you asking again?
When you're watching TV or reading, do you find that you lose focus easily, have to re-read things, or get distracted by noises or thoughts?

Um, re-reading things? I don't know, honestly. Like I said, I don't really read much anymore, so it's hard to say. I guess if I'm reading an article on my phone, maybe? But usually I'm just scrolling. 

I did try to read this one article yesterday about the best way to clean grout, because the grout in my bathroom is driving me crazy. It's supposed to be white, but it's turned this weird grayish-yellow color. I tried using bleach, but then the whole apartment smelled like a swimming pool for two days. Barnaby hated it. He wouldn't even go in the bathroom to use his litter box, which was a whole other disaster. I ended up having to buy this special enzyme cleaner online to get the smell out of the rug. It was so expensive, like thirty dollars for a tiny bottle. And the shipping took forever because of that big storm out on the East Coast last week. My sister lives in Boston, and she said they got like two feet of snow. I can't even imagine. I grew up in Florida, so anything below sixty degrees feels like freezing to me. 

But, um... I'm sorry, I don't really know if I lose focus when I read. I just don't do it enough to notice.
When you watch TV or read something, even on your phone, do you find that you lose focus easily or have trouble staying interested in what you're doing?

Um, trouble staying interested? Well, I guess... I mean, the main reason I actually made this appointment is because of work. I'm a nurse, and on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. Like, I'll be in the middle of figuring out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps down the hall, or someone asks another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I have absolutely no idea what I was just doing. 

It's so frustrating because it's so loud on the unit. We got these new IV pumps a few months ago, and the alarm on them is so piercing. It sounds exactly like my microwave when it's done, which is super weird. I actually burned a bag of popcorn in my microwave last night because I thought it was the pump beeping and I just tuned it out. The whole apartment smells like burnt popcorn now, which is almost worse than the bleach smell. Barnaby was just staring at me like I was crazy. 

But yeah, the floor is just... there's always a noise or something happening. So I guess, yes? I get distracted really easily, especially at work. I don't know if that answers what you were asking about TV, though.
When you're watching TV or reading something, even on your phone, do you find that you lose focus or have trouble staying interested in what you're doing?

Um, I'm really not sure. I guess I just haven't noticed if I lose focus with that stuff? Like, if I have the TV on, I'm usually folding laundry or doing something else anyway, so I don't know if I'm losing focus or just busy. 

I did try to actually just sit and watch this baking competition show on Saturday. I love baking, even though I'm completely terrible at it. I tried making those little French macarons once and they literally turned into flat, chewy pancakes. You're supposed to whip the egg whites for a really specific amount of time, but I think my hand mixer is just broken. It makes this horrible rattling sound now, kind of like the engine in my car when I go over forty miles an hour. I really need to take it in to get looked at, but the mechanic I usually go to just moved his shop all the way out to the suburbs, and traffic on the interstate is always such a nightmare in the afternoons. 

But yeah, I honestly don't know if I have trouble staying interested in TV shows or things on my phone. I just haven't really paid attention to it.

When you're doing something that requires you to stay focused for a while—like listening to a lecture, attending a meeting, or even just following directions—do you find it hard to stay engaged or often zone out?

Um, listening to a lecture or a meeting? I don't really know. I haven't really noticed if I zone out during that kind of stuff. We do have staff huddles on the floor, but they're usually pretty quick. We did have a big mandatory training last month in the main conference room, though, and honestly, I don't even know if I was engaged or not because the chairs in there are just horribly uncomfortable. They're those stiff plastic ones that totally ruin your posture. 

I actually just had to buy a new ergonomic chair for my desk at home because my lower back was killing me after my shifts. I ordered it from this place online, but it came in like a hundred different pieces. I swear, the instructions were completely impossible to follow. It reminded me of the last time I went to IKEA. I went just to get some of those little tea lights and ended up buying a whole bookshelf. And of course, I had to get the Swedish meatballs at the cafeteria while I was there. They're so good, especially with that lingonberry jam. My mom used to make something kind of similar when I was a kid, but she used cranberry sauce instead, which is a little too sweet for me. 

But, um... what were we talking about? Oh, zoning out in meetings. Yeah, I'm really not sure. I just try to get through them, I guess, so I haven't really paid attention to my focus.

Can you recall any situations outside of work—like when you're at home, running errands, or engaging in a hobby—where you find yourself struggling to stay focused or frequently losing your train of thought?

Um, outside of work? Like running errands and stuff? I honestly haven't really noticed if I do. I mean, when I go to the store, I just sort of go. I did run to Trader Joe's on Tuesday because they finally restocked those dark chocolate peanut butter cups I like, but the parking lot there is always just a complete disaster. People drive like absolute maniacs. This one guy in a silver Honda almost backed right into my cart while I was walking in. 

It totally reminded me of when I lived in Chicago for nursing school and I had to park on the street every day. Parallel parking in the snow is literally the worst thing in the world. My old roommate, Sarah, she wouldn't even try. She'd just drive around for like an hour until she found a spot she could pull straight into. She was so funny. She actually adopted a greyhound that was retired from racing, and that dog was just the biggest couch potato. You'd think a racing dog would have so much energy, right? But he just slept all day on this giant orthopedic bed. Barnaby is kind of like that, honestly, unless he hears a can open. I really need to get him one of those special deshedding brushes, though, because there's orange fur all over my couch.

But, um... yeah, I don't really know if I struggle to stay focused when I'm just at home or out doing things. I just haven't really thought about it outside of the hospital, so I'm not sure.

Can you think of any times, either at home, while running errands, or doing something else, where you start a task but then have trouble finishing it because your mind wanders or you get distracted easily?

Um, starting a task and not finishing it because I get distracted? Well, honestly, the main reason I actually made this appointment is because of what happens at work. On the floor, I lose my train of thought constantly. Like, I'll be in the middle of figuring out a patient flow issue, and then an IV pump beeps down the hall, or someone asks another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and suddenly I've completely forgotten what I was just doing. 

It’s so frustrating. Like yesterday, I was trying to chart, and the call light went off for room 12. The guy in there, Mr. Henderson, he's so sweet, he really is, but he hits that button for everything. He reminds me of my grandpa, honestly. My grandpa used to ring this little silver bell whenever he wanted my grandma to bring him iced tea. She’d get so mad, but she always did it. She made the best iced tea, too—she put fresh mint from her garden in it. I tried growing mint on my balcony last summer, but it completely took over the whole planter and choked out my basil. I was so sad because I love making homemade pesto. You really need pine nuts for a good pesto, but they're so ridiculously expensive at the grocery store right now. I saw a tiny little bag for like nine dollars the other day. 

But, um, yeah, at work, I just... I get sidetracked by every little noise or interruption, and I just can't hold onto my train of thought to finish what I was doing.

Can you think of any times when you're at home or doing something outside of work where you start a task—like cooking, cleaning, or even just responding to a text—and then realize you never finished it because you got distracted or lost track of what you were doing?

Um, starting something at home and not finishing it? Like cleaning or texting? I don't really know, to be honest. I haven't really noticed if I do that kind of stuff when I'm not at the hospital. I mean, when I'm off shift, I just try to decompress, you know? I did try to do laundry on Sunday, but my washing machine has been making this awful clanking noise during the spin cycle. It sounds like someone threw a handful of rocks in there. 

I really need to call my landlord about it, but he is just the hardest person to get ahold of. Last time I tried to call him, his voicemail was full, and he didn't text me back for like three days. And when he finally did, he sent this weird string of emojis that didn't even make sense. My dad is kind of like that with texting. He just discovered GIFs, so now every time I text him, he replies with a Minion GIF. It's kind of cute, but also a little exhausting. He sent me one yesterday of a Minion dropping a birthday cake, but it wasn't even my birthday. My birthday isn't until October. I'm actually thinking about going to Salem this year for Halloween since my birthday is so close to it. I've always wanted to see all the witchy stuff they do up there. I heard it gets super crowded, though, so I'd probably have to book an Airbnb like right now. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, getting distracted and not finishing things at home. Yeah, I really couldn't tell you. I just haven't really paid attention to it outside of work, so I don't really have an answer for that.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of difficulty maintaining focus, being easily distracted, and losing their train of thought across multiple settings (especially work, but also suggesting possible issues outside of work through indirect examples) most consistently align with ADHD, specifically predominantly inattentive presentation (F90.0). Other candidates (F06.7, F43.22, F07.81) were ruled out due to lack of evidence for organic mental disorder, adjustment disorder with anxiety or depression, or post-concussional syndrome.
